clue.text: Almost from the start, English piece of text getting bad score on course

indicators.note: Almost asks for the Latin phrase to lose its final letter, stopping just short of complete

parts.note: ab ovo is Latin for 'from the egg', i.e. from the very beginning
par. is an abbreviation for paragraph, a piece of text

explanation.surface: An English essay begun almost from scratch earns a poor mark, mixed up with golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims AB OVO (Latin, from the beginning) to ABOV. In golf a score above par means more strokes than standard, which is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, taking more strokes than the standard for a course is a poor result, so that phrase describes a bad score.

clue.text: From here, south of river, take New York line north

indicators.note: in a down clue, being south of something means coming below it, so these letters follow the river

parts.note: a brook is a small river or stream

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so New York line is turned around

explanation.surface: Directions for a commuter: from this spot south of the river, catch the New York subway line heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a travel tip from a New York borough; 'here' is that borough, lying south of the East River from Manhattan. 'take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is spoken from a place, and 'here' names that New York borough, the speaker's location.

clue.text: Asians in struggle, awfully tense after American invasion

indicators.note: after places the struggle word first, with the rest following it

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: invasion means the American abbreviation pushes its way into the jumbled letters
awfully suggests the word tense has been treated badly and reshaped

explanation.surface: A tense struggle in Asia made worse by an American invasion, recalling the war of the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles TENSE to TNESE, and the American 'invasion' breaks into that jumble; 'after' sets the struggle word in front. The surface recalls the Vietnam War.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Vietnam, a country in South-East Asia, are Asians.

clue.text: Ill-treated, essentially shortened by editor

parts.note: per se is a Latin phrase meaning in itself, essentially
cut means shortened, as a text is

explanation.surface: Complaining that one's work has been mistreated, mainly by being cut down by an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: PER SE is Latin for 'in itself', so it can stand for 'essentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone persecuted has been harassed or treated cruelly, so ill-treated is a synonym.

clue.text: Considers a well-wisher's utterance

definitions.meaning: to regard something is to look on or consider it
kind ... is a friendly closing sent by someone wishing you well

explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to consider, and best wishes sent at the end of a letter are this greeting.

clue.text: Gemstone in ring friend's holding up

indicators.note: in a down clue the friend holds up the ring by sitting beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
a pal is a friend; the 's is a contraction of 'is'

explanation.surface: A friend's ring has a precious stone set in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the piece below supports the one above, so PAL holding up O gives O then PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky, iridescent mineral is a well-known precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Go for very musical line

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai

explanation.surface: Someone opting for an extremely tuneful lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is to attack them, which is exactly what assail means.

clue.text: Yet Pooh gets excited about new treat for him

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the single new letter
gets excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh grows excited over a fresh treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets excited' rearranges YETPOOH, and 'about' wraps those letters round N. Pooh bear famously adores a pot of honey, so 'him' is Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar of honey is the favourite treat of Pooh, the bear in the children's stories.

clue.text: Strong drink, say, and nothing more

parts.note: to express something is to say it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A request for a strong drink, just that and nothing extra.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling with an X is an accepted variant of the Italian coffee name.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, concentrated shot of coffee is a strong drink.

clue.text: Problem about university affected person

indicators.note: about here means the problem word goes around the university letter

parts.note: a poser is a difficult problem or question

explanation.surface: A tricky issue concerning a university pretentious type.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts on airs to impress others is a pretentious, affected person.

clue.text: Use hammer in second room, making slow progress

indicators.note: in puts the hammering word inside the second-plus-room pair

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move
to nail something is to use a hammer on it

explanation.surface: A DIY job hammering in a spare room goes very slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes moving at the crawl of a garden mollusc, i.e. very slowly.

clue.text: Statement in court sure lacking in good feeling

indicators.note: lacking means the following word is missing from the feeling word

parts.note: pleasure is a good feeling

explanation.surface: A courtroom testimony that is uncertain and lacks goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sure' is the word removed, not part of the definition: PLEASURE without SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a court, a defendant's formal answer to a charge, such as guilty or not guilty, is called this.

clue.text: Moonshine or beer from some in school?

parts.note: a school of fish might contain some cod, which pluralises to give the possessive-looking piece
wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A question about schoolboys sneaking illicit liquor or beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a school of fish, not a place of learning. WALLOP is British slang for beer; Moonshine here means nonsense, not illicit spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean foolish talk, and this British slang word also means nonsense.

clue.text: Law's letter abused in financial centre

indicators.note: abused suggests the words are mistreated and so reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A legal letter misused in the world of finance.
explanation.definitionFit: This New York street is home to the stock exchange and is a byword for the US financial centre.

clue.text: Writing American volume, a true novel

parts.note: liter is the US spelling of litre, a unit of volume

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, signalling the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: An American book: a novel that is true to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges A TRUE into ATURE. It looks like a noun for a book, which suits the definition, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Written works collectively, such as books and poems, are called this.

clue.text: Penetrating and occupying part of France by end of March

parts.note: in means occupying, as being in a place
a French département, abbreviated dept, is an administrative region

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of March

explanation.surface: An account of an army occupying part of France by the end of March.
explanation.walkthrough: France is divided into départements, shortened to DEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A penetrating analysis goes deep into the subject, so it is thorough and detailed.

clue.text: Men fighting with home supporter subject to legal process

parts.note: in means at home
a fan is a supporter
to try someone is to put them on trial in court

explanation.surface: Soldiers with a fan at home facing a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers are men who fight on foot, collectively called this.

clue.text: Some excel — it is those one snobbishly prefers

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people excel, and those are the ones a snob favours.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob who favours the select few, the best people, is described by this word.

clue.text: Spot link, damaged, that's easily undone

indicators.note: damaged suggests the words are broken and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A weak spot in a chain link that has been damaged and comes apart.
explanation.definitionFit: This knot is designed to come loose with a pull, so it is easily untied.

clue.text: Is husband, after a kiss, ready for dinner?

indicators.note: after puts the kiss before the rest

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Is a husband, after kissing his wife, ready to eat?
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling peckish means slightly hungry, so ready for a meal.

clue.text: Socially isolated, not stopping at the end of the day

indicators.note: at the end of the places the never-ending word after the day

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
endless means going on without stopping

explanation.surface: Someone lonely, never stopping work even at the close of day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of the day' looks like the stock phrase meaning ultimately, but it splits: the never-ending word comes after the abbreviated weekday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no companions at all is lonely and cut off from society.

clue.text: Know instinctively, as people in cold area, about temperature

indicators.note: about means the Arctic people surround the temperature letter

parts.note: the Inuit are indigenous people of the Arctic

explanation.surface: Arctic peoples know by instinct what the temperature is.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something by intuition, without reasoning, is to know it instinctively.

clue.text: Nobody's work cut back in Stock Exchange activity

indicators.note: back means the shortened book title is read in reverse
cut means the final letter is chopped off

parts.note: The Diary of a Nobody is a comic novel by George and Weedon Grossmith

explanation.surface: A nobody's job reduced in the City, returning to the Stock Exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims DIARY to DIAR; 'back' turns that into the answer. A dawn raid is a sudden buying of shares in a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden attempt to buy up a company's shares on the market is called this.

clue.text: Ballet fanatic takes the biscuit

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a sports nut
a cracker is a crisp savoury biscuit

explanation.surface: An extreme enthusiast does something outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous, but here it supplies the biscuit word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's Christmas ballet is known by this name.

clue.text: It's a very old wicket, so declare

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket captain decides it is an ancient pitch and declares the innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'declare' is when a captain ends an innings early, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly or declare something.

clue.text: Queen I moved around, like knight?

indicators.note: moved around suggests the letters are shifted into a new arrangement, like pieces on a board

explanation.surface: A chess queen moves around in the manner of a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved around' rearranges QUEENI. A chess knight is shaped like a horse, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess knight is a horse's head, so a horse-like thing can be described as this.

clue.text: Much more than rose-tinted spectacles, naturally

definitions.text: Much more than rose-tinted spectacles, naturally

parts.words: Much more than rose-tinted spectacles, naturally
parts.note: rather than glasses tinted pink, think of natural sky displays showing many more colours than just rose

explanation.definitionFit: A natural sky arc shows a whole spectrum of colours, far more than just rose.

clue.text: Male with right to strike first, until now

indicators.note: first places the striking word ahead of the rest

parts.note: to hit is to strike
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man claiming the right to throw the first punch, as he always has.
explanation.definitionFit: This formal adverb is a synonym meaning up to the present time.
